{{Quote|Your primary objective is to locate civilians and get them to an evacuation ship.|Jedi Master Lar Le'Ung, regarding the Bulwarks' role in the evacuation of Rychel|<ref name="Invasion: Refugees 3" />}}
The '''Bulwark Mark III''', also known as the '''''Bulwark''-class battlecruiser''', was a massive [[Warship/Legends|warship]] developed by [[TransGalMeg Industries, Incorporated|TransGalMeg Industries]] using an old [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] [[Bulwark Mark I|battleship]] from the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] as a design basis. Equipped with extensive firepower, [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielding]], and carrying capacity, the 2,500-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] Bulwark Mark III was ideal for large-scale operations, capable of inflicting damage equal to an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Bulwark battlecruiser was one of the most heavily [[Armor/Legends|armored]] and durable [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] serving with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], while the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation's]] [[Sullustan Home Guard/Legends|Sullustan Home Guard]] also utilized the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] in defense of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]]. Later, during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] employed several Bulwarks in an operation to help [[Evacuation of Rychel|evacuate]] citizens from the beleaguered planet [[Rychel]], which had fallen under [[Yuuzhan Vong]] attack, and again during a [[Battle of Shramar|blockade]] to defend the planet [[Shramar]] from Vong invasion.

==Characteristics==
Developed by [[TransGalMeg Industries, Incorporated]],<ref name="CSWE" /> the Bulwark Mark III,<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> or ''Bulwark''-class [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]],<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> was a massive,<ref name="CSWE" /> 2,500-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> [[Capital ship/Legends|capital]] [[Warship/Legends|warship]]. Although plagued by rumors of unreliable electronics and [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], the Bulwark Mark III nevertheless boasted an extensive arsenal, [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielding]], and carrying capacity.<ref name="CSWE" /> Armed with several [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]], [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], and outfitted with a support complement of up to ten [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] and four [[Troop/Legends|troop]] [[Regiment/Legends|regiments]], the Bulwark was a veritable mobile fortress.<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion" /> Adding to its versatility, the immense battlecruiser was capable of making [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] landfall and disembarking ground forces.<ref name="Invasion: Refugees 3" /> The Bulwark was equipped with a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] system in addition to a basic [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight drive]].<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 5" />

==Role==
The Bulwark Mark III's powerful armaments and considerable defensive capabilities made it ideal for large-scale military operations.<ref name="CSWE" /> The battlecruiser could absorb and administer damage equal to that of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]].<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" />

==History==
===Age of Rebellion===
TransGalMeg Industries developed the Bulwark Mark III based on the old designs of the [[Bulwark Mark I]],<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare-Note">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' states that [[TransGalMeg Industries, Incorporated|TransGalMeg Industries]] built the Bulwark Mark III "using the old [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] design as a starting point." According to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', the Techno Union developed the [[Bulwark Mark I]], thereby identifying the Bulwark Mark III's design inspiration. Note that the [[Bulwark Mark II]]'s developer was never identified in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]].</ref> a behemoth warship produced by the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] and later used by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The Bulwark Mark III directly succeeded the [[Bulwark Mark II]], another Clone Wars&ndash;era Confederate [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]].<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" />

During the subsequent [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion" /> the Bulwark Mark III proved to be one of the most [[Armor/Legends|armored]], durable,<ref name="CSWE" /> and battle-proof [[Starship/Legends|starships]] employed by the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]].<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion" /> Additionally, the [[Sullustan Home Guard/Legends|Sullustan Home Guard]], an [[Pirate/Legends|antipiracy]] [[Fleet/Legends|armada]] established by the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]] to defend the planet [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], also utilized the Bulwark Mark III during this period.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" />

{{RPGseed}}
Shortly before the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the SoroSuub [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] constructed the Bulwark battlecruiser ''[[Arrow of Sullust]]''. However, SoroSuub&mdash;formally neutral during the Galactic Civil War but secretly sympathetic to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] in its struggle against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]&mdash;could not openly deliver the ship to the Rebellion. The task of stealing the Bulwark thus fell to a group of Rebels, who, with only a skeleton crew, held off Imperial forces long enough to cruise to a safe distance and escape to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] with the ''Arrow of Sullust''.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" />
{{Endgame}}

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
{{Quote|Strike force, the wait is over. Return, and hit your targets with ''everything'' you've got.|Admiral [[Bylsma]] relates Queen Galfridian's order to attack the Yuuzhan Vong supply fields on Shramar|<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 5" />}}
[[File:FinnHelpsRefugees-Invasion3.png|thumb|left|280px|Bulwark Mark III battlecruisers evacuate refugees from Rychel during the Yuuzhan Vong War.]]
TransGalMeg later constructed Bulwark Mark IIIs for the burgeoning [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Rebel Alliance's successor state, early in its existence.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], amidst the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the New Republic dispatched at least four Bulwarks to assist in the [[Evacuation of Rychel|evacuation]] of the besieged planet [[Rychel]], whose civilians had fallen under attack by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. The Bulwarks delivered a joint force of [[New Republic soldier/Legends|Republic troops]] and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Masters]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Lar Le'Ung]] to Rychel's surface to [[Ground warfare/Legends|combat]] the Vong and evacuate as many civilians as possible aboard the battlecruisers. Once filled with Rychel evacuees, the Bulwarks departed the planet with the surviving Jedi and Republic forces, although many civilians were left behind at the mercy of the Yuuzhan Vong, as the New Republic did not have the resources to evacuate everyone.<ref name="Invasion: Refugees 3" />

Later in 25 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]], at least two Bulwarks participated in the joint New Republic&ndash;[[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial]] [[Battle of Shramar|blockade]] of the planet [[Shramar]], an effort to prevent the [[Yuuzhan Vong fleet]] from recovering its captured [[slaveship]], the ''[[Heart of Artorias]]'', which the Republic and Imperials were using on the surface to evacuate refugees from the planet. The [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]], however, eventually became part of a larger plan masterminded by [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Nina Galfridian]] of the planet [[Artorias]] to destroy the Yuuzhan Vong's vital supply fields on Shramar. As the Vong attack on Shramar began, Galfridian ordered the joint Republic&ndash;Imperial fleet to withdraw into hyperspace and wait, a diversionary move. Convinced the planetary defenders had retreated in defeat, the Vong moved in to attack the ''Heart of Artorias''. At that moment Galfridian ordered her ships to return to Shramar. The Bulwarks and the rest of the fleet arrived on the other side of the planet from the Vong force and unleashed a devastating [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] that wiped out the enemy supply fields before once more escaping into hyperspace and later [[Outer Rim Alliance|rendezvousing]] at the edge of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 5" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Good catch on the Bulwark battlecruiser from the game ''Rebellion''. Note that this is actually the 'Bulwark Mark I,' however. It's still definitely a ''Rebellion'' tie-in, but I wanted to make sure I depowered the ship enough for it to fit into the Clone Wars timeframe.|Daniel Wallace discusses the Bulwark's inclusion in ''The New Essential Chronology''|<ref name="JCF1">{{JCFCite|url=posts/22088879|board=Literature|thread=The Official Daniel Wallace Discussion Thread|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]]|date=2005-10-26|time=8:02 PM}}</ref>}}
The Bulwark Mark III first appeared in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|PC game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] as one of the playable capital ships available to the Rebel Alliance. Referred to in the game as the "Bulwark Battlecruiser," and by the in-game encyclopedia as the "Bulwark class capital ship," the Bulwark represents the game's most powerful warship in the Alliance arsenal, designed to be a competitive match for the Galactic Empire's [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] in gameplay.<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion" /> As the Bulwark's entry in the [[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Rebellion'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]] notes, "the Bulwark battlecruiser is the most powerful in the game and can stand toe-to-toe with all Imperial ships except the Death Star [&hellip;] this battlecruiser is almost a fleet in and of itself. It's the natural flagship for any major Alliance fleet."<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion: Guide">[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Rebellion'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref>

[[File:Bulwarks-Invasion3.png|thumb|right|250px|Bulwark battlecruisers, as illustrated in the comic ''Invasion'' 3]]
The Bulwark from ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' later received a nod in the [[2005]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', which refers to a "Bulwark Mark I" vessel utilized by the Techno Union during the Clone Wars.<ref name="TNEC" /> Author [[Daniel Wallace]] explained that he intended this vessel to be a ''Rebellion'' tie-in, as a sort of Clone Wars&ndash;era predecessor to the ''Rebellion'' Bulwark battlecruiser.<ref name="JCF1" /> Wallace further speculated on the ''Rebellion'' Bulwark's exact relation to his Bulwark Mark I: "I'll allow that they could be Mark IIIs or IVs, depending on whether anyone ever goes back to create new ship classes. I've always thought that the New Republic got their hands on Bulwarks at some point post-[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|ROJ]], but that the Rebel Alliance never did."<ref name="JCF2">{{JCFCite|url=posts/22148813|board=Literature|thread=The Official Daniel Wallace Discussion Thread|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]]|date=2005-10-31|time=9:08 AM}}</ref>

In [[2008]], the ''Rebellion'' Bulwark was granted an official starship classification with the release of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', which identified the vessel as the "''Bulwark''-class battle cruiser," drawing upon the original in-game encyclopedia entry material from ''Star Wars: Rebellion''.<ref name="CSWE" /> Author [[Jason Fry]], who has collaborated with Daniel Wallace on several previous ''[[Star Wars]]'' works,<ref name="Hoth and the Greater Javin">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040325web|text=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin|int=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin}}</ref><ref name="Rough and Tundra">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040325adv|text=Rough and Tundra|int=Rough and Tundra}}</ref><ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> included the ''Rebellion'' Bulwark in his [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', in which he established the vessel's name as the "Bulwark Mark III" and described it as being built by TransGalMeg Industries for the New Republic.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Fry intended to [[canon]]ize Wallace's plans for the evolution of the ''Rebellion'' Bulwark class, which Wallace had previously discussed but had never had an opportunity to do so.<ref name="Jason Fry e-mail">{{EmailCite|email=Wookieepedia:Email/Jason Fry (2012)|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2012-12-12}}</ref> However, given that Wallace's evolution is inconsistent with ''Star Wars: Rebellion'', ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'', and the [[2015]] [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion (roleplaying game)|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'']] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]'', all of which state that the Rebel Alliance utilized the Bulwark, this article attempts to reconcile all information.
